faq.a: Gunay is associated with the Turkic form غُونَاي, whose core sense is gunay; sun and moon (turkic).

faq.q: What is the origin of Gunay?
faq.a: Gunay is associated with Turkic. Gunay is a Turkic (Azerbaijani) female given name, from gün ('day, sun') + ay ('moon').
No — the underlying form is Turkic, not Arabic.
Gunay can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Gunay should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Günay is a Turkic compound, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Gunay mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Gunay is rendered گنائے and carries the sense گنائے، سورج اور چاند.

faq.q: What does Gunay mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Gunay is rendered گونای and carries the sense گونای، خورشید و ماه.
A romanized syllable approximation is gu-nay. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Gunay?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Gunay, gunay. Script forms are غُونَاي, ګوناي, گنائے, گونای, गुनाय.

faq.q: Is Gunay a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
